title: Reinforcement learning
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how agents learn from reward: multi-armed bandits and exploration, Markov decision processes and the Bellman equations, dynamic programming with policy and value iteration, Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning, Q-learning and SARSA, function approximation and deep Q-networks, policy gradients and actor-critic methods, model-based reinforcement learning and planning, and the safety problems of reward-driven systems.
primary_reading: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd edition, by Sutton and Barto (free PDF)

weeks.2: Upper confidence bounds and Thompson sampling
weeks.5: Dynamic programming: policy evaluation and policy iteration
weeks.12: Model-based reinforcement learning, planning and the safety problems of reward

blocks.deliverable: Run epsilon-greedy and UCB on a simulated bandit and compare their regret.
Write the Bellman equations for a small MDP and solve them.
Run value iteration on a gridworld.
Week 7 midterm; compare Monte Carlo and TD estimates on a random walk.
Train a Q-learning agent on a small grid with hazards.
Derive the REINFORCE update and run it on a bandit.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Gridworld agents: implement value iteration, Monte Carlo control, SARSA and Q-learning in plain Python for a supplied gridworld with hazards, compare their learned policies and learning curves (as tables), test how each handles a change in the reward, and write a report that includes one example of an agent exploiting a badly specified reward.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
